questions.question:
Let \( f: R \rightarrow R \), satisfy \( f(x+y)=2^{x} f(y)+4^{y} f(x), \forall x, y \in R \). If \( f(2)=3 \), then \( 14 \cdot \frac{f^{\prime}(4)}{f^{\prime}(2)} \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 June (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The functional equation is \(f(x+y)=2^xf(y)+4^yf(x)\).

Putting \(x=0\) and \(y=0\),

\(f(0)=f(0)+f(0)\),

so \(f(0)=0\)

Now interchange \(x\) and \(y\). We get

\(f(x+y)=2^yf(x)+4^xf(y)\)

Equating the two expressions for \(f(x+y)\),

\(2^xf(y)+4^yf(x)=2^yf(x)+4^xf(y)\)

Therefore, \((4^x-2^x)f(y)=(4^y-2^y)f(x)\)

For non-zero \(x\) and \(y\),

\(\dfrac{f(x)}{4^x-2^x}=\dfrac{f(y)}{4^y-2^y}\)

Hence, this ratio is a constant. Let the constant be \(C\).

Then, \(f(x)=C(4^x-2^x)\)

This formula also gives \(f(0)=0\), so it is valid at \(x=0\).

Using \(f(2)=3\),

\(3=C(4^2-2^2)\)

\(=C(16-4)\)

\(=12C\)

Therefore, \(C=\dfrac14\)

Thus, \(f(x)=\dfrac14(4^x-2^x)\)

Differentiating,

\(f'(x)=\dfrac14\left(4^x\log_e4-2^x\log_e2\right)\)

Since \(\log_e4=2\log_e2\),

\(f'(x)=\dfrac{\log_e2}{4}(2\cdot4^x-2^x)\)

Therefore,

\(f'(4)=\dfrac{\log_e2}{4}(2\cdot256-16)\)

\(=\dfrac{\log_e2}{4}(496)\)

\(=124\log_e2\)

Also,

\(f'(2)=\dfrac{\log_e2}{4}(2\cdot16-4)\)

\(=\dfrac{\log_e2}{4}(28)\)

\(=7\log_e2\)

Hence,

\(14\cdot\dfrac{f'(4)}{f'(2)}=14\cdot\dfrac{124\log_e2}{7\log_e2}\)

\(=14\cdot\dfrac{124}{7}=248\)

Let a line \( L_{1} \) be tangent to the hyperbola \( \frac{x^{2}}{16}-\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1 \) and let \( L_{2} \) be the line passing through the origin and perpendicular to \( L_{1} \). If the locus of the point of intersection of \( L_{1} \) and \( L_{2} \) is \(\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}=\alpha x^{2}+ \) \( \beta y^{2} \), then \( \alpha+\beta \) is equal to________

questions.explanation:
Let the tangent to \(\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1\) at \((x_1,y_1)\) be

\(\dfrac{xx_1}{16}-\dfrac{yy_1}{4}=1\)

Write it as

\(Ax+By=1\)

where \(A=\dfrac{x_1}{16}\) and \(B=-\dfrac{y_1}{4}\).

Let \((x,y)\) be the foot of the perpendicular from the origin to this tangent.

For the line \(Ax+By=1\),

\(x=\dfrac{A}{A^2+B^2}\)

\(y=\dfrac{B}{A^2+B^2}\)

Thus,

\(A=\dfrac{x}{x^2+y^2}\)

\(B=\dfrac{y}{x^2+y^2}\)

\(x_1=\dfrac{16x}{x^2+y^2}\)

\(y_1=-\dfrac{4y}{x^2+y^2}\)

Using \(\dfrac{x_1^2}{16}-\dfrac{y_1^2}{4}=1\),

\(\dfrac{16x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}-\dfrac{4y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}=1\)

\((x^2+y^2)^2=16x^2-4y^2\)

Comparing with \((x^2+y^2)^2=\alpha x^2+\beta y^2\),

\(\alpha=16\)

\(\beta=-4\)

\(\therefore \alpha+\beta=12\)

questions.question:
The mean and standard deviation of 40 observations are 30 and 5 respectively. It was noticed that two of these observations 12 and 10 were wrongly recorded. If \( \sigma \) is the standard deviation of the data after omitting the two wrong observations from the data, then \( 38 \sigma^{2} \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For the original \(40\) observations, \(\sum x_i=40\times 30=1200\).

Using \(\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n}-\bar{x}^{\,2}\), we get \(\sum x_i^2=40(5^2+30^2)=37000\).

After omitting \(12\) and \(10\), the number of observations is \(38\).

\(\Rightarrow \text{New sum}=1200-12-10=1178\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{New mean}=\dfrac{1178}{38}=31\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{New sum of squares}=37000-12^2-10^2=36756\)

\(\Rightarrow \sigma^2=\dfrac{36756}{38}-31^2=\dfrac{119}{19}\)

\(\Rightarrow 38\sigma^2=38\times\dfrac{119}{19}=238\)

The required value is \(238\).
